problems.title: Stencil intensity
problems.statement: 7-point stencil, FP32, 13 FLOPs per point, minimum traffic one read and one write.

problems.title: 3-D tile halos
problems.statement: A block of 1,024 threads loads a T³ tile with a halo of 1 (one point per thread).

parts.prompt: Fraction of loaded points that are outputs, in %?

problems.solution: T = 8: 512 of 1,000 loaded points are outputs, 51%. 3-D halos are expensive.

problems.title: Register tiling along z
problems.statement: Thread coarsening in z keeps z − 1, z, z + 1 in registers; x/y neighbours come from global memory (cache).

parts.prompt: With the current plane also in shared memory?

problems.title: Parallelism after coarsening
problems.statement: N = 512 grid, 32 × 32 thread tiles over (x, y), each thread walking C_z planes. GPU holds 32,768 threads at once.

parts.prompt: With C_z = 8 at N = 32: threads launched?

problems.solution: (a) 262,144 threads at N = 512: plenty of parallelism even coarsened over all of z. (b) At N = 32 with C_z = 8: 4,096 threads, an eighth of what the GPU can hold, so latency isn't hidden; that's why the simulator's coarsened kernel only wins at N = 64.

problems.title: Temporal blocking
problems.statement: A tile advances k time steps in shared memory before writing back. Each step needs a halo of 1 more point.

parts.prompt: DRAM traffic per point per time step, relative to one step at a time, for k = 4 (ignoring halo)?
2-D tile of 32 × 32 outputs after k = 4 steps: input tile side?

hints: Read once, write once per k steps.
problems.solution: (a) 1/k = 0.25. (b) 40 × 40: the halo grows by 1 per step per side, so temporal blocking trades redundant halo work for DRAM traffic.

problems.title: Higher order
problems.statement: A 13-point stencil reads 2 neighbours in each direction (±1, ±2).

parts.prompt: With z register tiling (5 z-values in registers)?

problems.solution: 13 → 9; the saving grows with stencil order, which is why seismic codes tile along z.

problems.title: Bandwidth bound
problems.statement: One Jacobi step of a 512³ FP32 grid on a 1 TB/s GPU.

parts.prompt: Minimum time per step, in ms?

problems.solution: 1.07 ms per step; 1.07 s for 1,000 steps: temporal blocking is the only way past this.

problems.title: Choosing coarsening

options: When the naive grid has more threads than the GPU holds
When it removes redundant loads or work
When the grid is already too small to fill the GPU
When it increases registers past the occupancy cliff

problems.solution: Coarsen when parallelism is in surplus and the merged work shares data; not when it starves the GPU or spills.

problems.title: Shared-plane variant
problems.statement: A 32 × 32 thread tile stages the current z-plane (with x/y halos) in shared memory each step.

parts.prompt: Floats loaded per step per block (plane tile with halo)?

hints: The 4 corners aren't needed by a 7-point stencil.
problems.solution: 1152 loads for 1,024 outputs: 1.12 per point, against 7 naive.
